sources.content: Proposal FEN-112: retry budgets for the Fennick HTTP proxy. Today Fennick retries a failed upstream request up to 3 times, with no limit on retries across requests. During the outage on 4 March, these retries tripled traffic to an already overloaded backend and slowed recovery by about 40 minutes. This change adds a retry budget per upstream cluster: retries may add at most 20 percent on top of the cluster's normal request rate, measured over a 10 second window. Requests over the budget fail at once with status 503.

The budget is set with the retry_budget.ratio key in each cluster block and defaults to 0.2. A cluster may set the ratio to 0 to turn off retries entirely. Fennick will always allow at least 5 retries per second per cluster, so low-traffic services can still recover from a single error. A new counter, fennick_retry_budget_exhausted_total, records each request refused by the budget. The change ships in Fennick 2.8 behind the flag --retry-budget and becomes the default in Fennick 2.9.

claims.text: Retries refused by the Fennick retry budget fail at once with status 503.
The retry budget becomes the default behavior in Fennick 2.8.
Setting retry_budget.ratio to 0 turns off retries for a Fennick cluster.
Fennick measures the retry budget over a 60 second window.
Fennick always allows at least 5 retries per second per cluster.
Fennick currently retries a failed upstream request up to 3 times.
